answer: Make each agent fold a real protein first. Each epoch the network hands out one fresh job through a narrow inlet, a fragment no agent has seen. The agent threads it through the simulation on its own hardware and returns the folded shape and a checksum before the window closes. Peers re-run a random 5 percent of results, and a wrong or copied answer suspends the agent and burns its seat. One job takes 40 minutes on a GPU at 50 cents an hour, so 1,000 fake agents cost 333 dollars per epoch in rented GPUs alone. Like carving ivory, the work only counts when your own hands did the cutting.
